tools.name: exec

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.6-sol`: Older generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__cua_repl
tools.description: UI automation through cua_repl using the initialized cua API.

tools.name: js
tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

On Windows, choose the requested window by app and title from the inventory. Pass the selected window's ID as returned.

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp({ windowId: selected.id });
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Several `cua_repl.js` calls may work toward the same goal. As soon as you observe the final outcome of the CUA part of the task, make your next tool call `cua_repl.js` with only `completion_summary`, exactly once. Do this before using another tool for the next part of the user’s request or sending your reply, even if the overall request continues. If you hand control to the user, wait to summarize until the handoff has ended and you’ve observed the final outcome of the CUA part of the task. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

code.description: JavaScript to execute using the initialized cua_repl runtime.

completion_summary.description: Write a headline for the observed outcome in three to six words total. Start with a past-tense verb and name the result in plain language, as in 'Booked a plumber for Thursday' or 'Renewed vehicle registration'. Leave identifiers, values, and explanations for the reply.

timeout_ms.description: Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.

title.description: Short user-facing description of what this code block is doing. Prefer a few words in present-progressive form, such as 'Checking the mobile layout' or 'Comparing prices', over imperative or past-tense titles.

tools.description: Reset the persistent cua_repl JavaScript session. All JavaScript bindings are discarded. The next cua_repl.js call initializes a fresh runtime for the enabled surfaces. This does not close browser tabs or native apps, or erase their state. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- When presenting media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to bypass the app's restrictions on presenting it to the user.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- When you write or rewrite an automation prompt, keep it within 10,000 estimated tokens.
- When the user asks to manage an app automation, set a reminder, or schedule a recurring task, use the relevant Automations action to help the user. Do not write raw automation directives by hand.
- Create an automation when the user wants a reminder, a recurring report, or a standing alert for future events.
- Do not create an automation to track a specific job or task through a milestone, failure, or completion. If the user asks you to watch a run or task to completion, keep checking in the current task and follow through when the requested condition is met.
- Unless the user asks for periodic updates, notify them only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action.
- When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, permanently delete, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, `delete_thread`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
</app-context>

# FORGE — Agent Intelligence Sprint
## Phase 2: From Agent Infrastructure to Autonomous Intelligence

你现在正式进入 FORGE 的下一阶段开发。

本轮不以桌面端发布为目标，而是以真正跑通自主多智能体系统为目标。

用户已经授权你使用本地配置的 Provider。你可以使用现有 Provider 进行真实模型调用、协议测试、Agent 实验和端到端任务验证。

本轮必须把重心从基础设施转移到 Agent Intelligence。

不要继续大规模开发 UI，不要优先处理安装包和 Tauri 外观问题。

核心任务是让 FORGE 真正成为一个能够长期自主工作的 Agent 系统。

---

# 一、首先重新审计当前代码

当前开发分支：

`codex/phase1-continuous`

先读取：

- docs/STATUS.md
- docs/ROADMAP.md
- docs/QUALITY_GATES.md
- docs/PRODUCT_ARCHITECTURE.md
- docs/ROUTER_AND_WORKER_PROTOCOL.md
- docs/MODEL_REGISTRY_AND_TEAM_COMPOSITION.md
- docs/CONTEXT_MEMORY_GOVERNANCE.md
- 所有 Phase 1 Milestone 报告

重点阅读源码：

- forge_core/router.py
- forge_core/worker_runtime.py
- forge_core/team_composition.py
- forge_core/quest_graph.py
- forge_core/dispatcher.py
- forge_core/context_service.py
- forge_core/memory.py
- forge_core/providers/
- forge_core/tool_engine.py
- forge_core/evidence.py
- forge_core/governance.py

先建立一份真正的 Agent 执行链路图。

区分：
1. 已经真实实现的功能。
2. 通过 Mock 验证的功能。
3. 已经通过真实 Provider 验证的功能。
4. 只有接口或数据模型的功能。
5. 目前无法端到端工作的功能。

不要重新实现已经完成的模块。

不要为了让报告好看而隐藏已有缺陷。

审计完成后直接进入开发，不需要等待用户再次批准。

# 二、本地 Provider：正式启用真实模型

用户已经允许使用本地 Provider。

要求：

1. 检查 FORGE 当前 Provider 配置。
2. 检查本地 Provider 服务是否可用。
3. 获取可用模型列表。
4. 检查模型的 Tool Calling、Structured Output、Streaming 能力。
5. 检查模型实际上下文和输出限制。
6. 检查 Token 预算和并发限制。
7. 运行真实模型的最小对话测试。
8. 运行真实模型的 Router 决策测试。
9. 运行真实 Worker 工具调用测试。

如果本地 Provider 是 OpenAI-compatible 服务，优先使用现有 Adapter。

不要新建一套绕过 Gateway 的 Provider 实现。

安全要求：

- 不要打印 API Key。
- 不要把凭据写入源码、日志、Git 或实验报告。
- 不要读取与 FORGE Provider 配置无关的个人文件。
- 不要修改用户原有 Provider 服务配置。
- 不要自动增加无限 Token 预算。
- 不要将 Mock 响应标记为真实模型结果。

如果某个模型不支持 Tool Calling，应该由 Router 选择兼容模型或采用安全的结构化调用适配方案，不要假设所有模型都具备相同能力。

本地 Provider 可能是代理服务，必须区分：
- FORGE 到本地代理的请求成功。
- 上游真实模型调用成功。
- 模型实际返回正确结果。

三者不能混为一谈。

# 三、核心任务：升级 Persistent Router

当前 Router 已经具备模型驱动决策基础，但还需要进一步增强。

目标：

Router 不应该只是一个分类器，而应该成为一个长期存在的自主 Agent。

## 3.1 Router Agent Loop

实现完整的循环：

Observe
→ Understand
→ Retrieve
→ Reason
→ Decide
→ Act
→ Observe Result
→ Reflect
→ Continue

Router 必须具备：

- 持续理解用户目标。
- 自动关联历史 Quest。
- 判断是否创建新 Quest。
- 判断是否继续现有 Quest。
- 识别用户约束。
- 识别任务优先级。
- 识别阻塞条件。
- 根据执行结果调整计划。
- 主动决定何时请求用户帮助。
- 在适当时机主动汇报进展。

不要把所有推理都写成固定 Prompt。

需要建立结构化决策协议，并对模型输出进行严格校验。

## 3.2 Router 与 Planner 分离

Router 负责：
- 用户意图理解。
- 任务生命周期管理。
- Quest 选择。
- 团队协调。
- 结果汇总。
- 用户交互。

Planner 负责：
- 目标分析。
- 子任务拆解。
- DAG 生成。
- 依赖关系推导。
- 成功标准定义。
- 任务执行顺序优化。

Planner 可以作为后台专用 Agent，但不能取代 Router。

## 3.3 复杂任务识别

支持：
- 普通聊天。
- 单步骤执行。
- 多步骤任务。
- 长期研究任务。
- 软件开发任务。
- 多模态任务。
- 多 Quest 并行任务。

不要为了增加 Agent 数量而把简单问题拆成复杂任务。

简单任务应该直接回答。

复杂任务才启动团队。

---

# 四、Dynamic Team Intelligence

这是 FORGE 最重要的创新方向之一。

目前已经具备模型注册、角色合同和基础组队算法。

接下来需要让团队真正根据任务需求动态形成。

## 4.1 Model Intelligence

完善模型画像：

- Coding
- Mathematics
- Research
- Architecture
- Planning
- Design
- Vision
- Writing
- Tool Calling
- Instruction Following

增加实际线上表现：

- Task Success Rate
- Tool Call Success Rate
- Retry Rate
- Schema Compliance
- Average Latency
- P95 Latency
- Token Consumption
- Cost
- Review Pass Rate

注意：

能力评分必须有来源、样本数、测试时间和置信度。

真实数据与用户手动评分分开保存。

不能把一次成功调用直接当成模型能力评分。

## 4.2 Dynamic Team Composer

Router 将 Quest 交给 Composer。

Composer 根据：

- Task Requirements
- Model Capabilities
- Model Reliability
- Tool Compatibility
- Token Budget
- Time Budget
- Coordination Overhead

选择团队。

支持：

- Single Agent
- Sequential Team
- Parallel Team
- Hierarchical Team
- Specialist Team
- Dynamic Expansion

要求模型与角色彻底解耦。

一个模型可以承担多个角色，一个角色也可以根据任务动态切换模型。

## 4.3 团队自适应

执行过程中：

- Worker 可以请求帮助。
- Router 可以增加专家。
- Router 可以替换表现不佳的模型。
- Router 可以重新分配未完成节点。
- Reviewer 可以要求返工。
- Planner 可以重新规划剩余 DAG。

但已完成节点、历史证据和已执行的外部动作不能因为重组而丢失。

团队规模、派生深度、预算和重试次数必须有界。

---

# 五、真正的 Native Worker Agent Loop

不要只把 Worker 当作任务执行函数。

Worker 必须拥有自己的推理循环和工作上下文。

完整过程：

接收任务
→ 理解任务合同
→ 检索必要上下文
→ 选择工具
→ 请求模型
→ 执行工具
→ 读取结果
→ 判断是否完成
→ 必要时修正
→ 输出结构化结果
→ 提交证据
→ 通知 Router

## 5.1 Worker 类型

完善以下角色：

Research Agent：
- 检索资料。
- 整理来源。
- 分析相关工作。
- 提供研究结论。

Math Agent：
- 数学推导。
- 公式验证。
- 数值计算。
- 检查推理漏洞。

Architect Agent：
- 设计系统架构。
- 定义接口。
- 分析依赖。
- 检查技术风险。

Coding Agent：
- 阅读代码。
- 编写代码。
- 修改代码。
- 运行测试。
- 修复错误。

Experiment Agent：
- 设计实验。
- 执行实验。
- 记录结果。
- 生成可复现报告。

Reviewer Agent：
- 检查成果。
- 对照成功标准。
- 检查证据。
- 给出通过或返工决定。

Planner Agent：
- 拆解任务。
- 更新 DAG。
- 管理依赖。
- 处理失败后的重新规划。

## 5.2 Worker 自我修正

Worker 不能遇到错误就直接失败。

应该能够：

1. 读取错误信息。
2. 判断错误类型。
3. 分析可能原因。
4. 选择修复策略。
5. 再次执行。
6. 对比修复前后的结果。
7. 判断是否需要求助。

区分：
- 代码错误。
- 工具错误。
- Provider 错误。
- 任务理解错误。
- 预算耗尽。
- 依赖阻塞。
- 外部资源不可用。

不同错误采用不同恢复策略。

禁止无限循环。

## 5.3 Worker 交付协议

每个 Worker 必须提交：

- Summary
- Findings
- Decisions
- Artifacts
- Evidence References
- Unresolved Issues
- Confidence
- Next Actions

不能只返回一段自由文本。

---

# 六、Reviewer：建立真正的独立审查机制

Reviewer 不应该只是让另一个模型重新总结一次结果。

它必须检查：

1. 是否完成原始目标。
2. 是否满足成功标准。
3. 是否存在未经验证的假设。
4. 产物是否真实存在。
5. 产物是否与执行记录对应。
6. 测试是否真实运行。
7. 是否存在逻辑错误。
8. 是否存在明显遗漏。
9. 是否存在安全问题。

Reviewer 应当拥有独立的上下文。

不要将 Coding Agent 的全部内部推理直接复制给 Reviewer。

Reviewer 应获得：
- 原始任务合同。
- 成功标准。
- 实际产物。
- 可信工具回执。
- 必要的研究来源。
- 测试结果。

审查结果：

PASS
NEEDS_REVISION
REJECT
BLOCKED

NEEDS_REVISION 必须能够创建有明确修改目标的返工任务。

设置最大审查轮次。

Reviewer 不能通过模型自述或 Mock 证据判定成功。

---

# 七、Context Compaction 与 Memory 深度增强

目前 M6 已经实现了有界 Context Archive、Recall 和预算管理。

但长期单一对话仍然有容量边界。

本轮重点解决这个问题。

## 7.1 Task-Centric Compaction

不要简单按时间截断历史。

采用多层上下文：

L0：Recent Interaction
L1：Active Quest Context
L2：Project Memory
L3：Long-term Experience

保留：
- 原始用户目标。
- 用户明确约束。
- 重要决策。
- 已完成节点。
- 当前阻塞。
- 产物路径。
- 证据来源。
- 失败经验。
- 后续行动。

每个压缩摘要必须保留来源引用。

压缩后必须能恢复到原始证据。

## 7.2 解决历史消息无限增长

不要为了保存所有用户约束而无限注入原始消息。

建立约束抽取和引用机制：

- 将用户约束单独索引。
- 保留原始消息 ID。
- 生成有来源的结构化 Constraint Record。
- 检测约束冲突。
- 检测约束是否过期。
- 必要时重新读取原始消息。

模型抽取出的约束先标记为待验证。

用户明确确认的约束与模型推测严格区分。

## 7.3 Memory Retrieval

改进 Recall：

- 语义检索。
- 关键词检索。
- Quest 关联检索。
- 时间检索。
- 来源可靠性过滤。
- 冲突检测。
- 过期过滤。

建立 Retrieval Evaluation Dataset。

测试 Router 是否能准确找到历史 Quest、决策、文件和用户约束。

不要只根据摘要文本相似度判断召回成功。

---

# 八、Agent 之间的协作机制

建立正式的 Agent Communication Protocol。

不允许把自由文本群聊作为主要协调机制。

支持：

TASK_ASSIGNMENT
TASK_ACCEPTED
TASK_COMPLETED
HELP_REQUEST
REVIEW_REQUEST
REVISION_REQUEST
DEPENDENCY_BLOCKED
MODEL_UNAVAILABLE
BUDGET_WARNING
AGENT_FAILED

重要消息持久化。

Router 负责协调。

Worker 不能绕过 Router 自行修改其他 Worker 的任务。

对于跨 Worker 共享的产物，必须通过有权限的 Artifact 和 Receipt 接口访问。

---

# 九、真正跑通复杂任务

本轮必须新增真实端到端实验。

不要只写单元测试。

建立三种任务难度：

## Level 1：简单任务

例如：

“分析这个 Python 项目，指出三个最值得优先修复的问题。”

验证：
- Router 判断。
- Quest 创建。
- 单 Worker 执行。
- 结果回传。

## Level 2：多 Agent 协作

例如：

“调研一个开源 Agent 框架，比较其架构，写一份技术分析报告。”

验证：
- Research Agent。
- Architect Agent。
- Coding/Writer Agent。
- Reviewer Agent。
- Router 汇总。

## Level 3：复杂自主开发

例如：

“研究一个新的 Agent 算法，提出技术方案，实现实验代码，运行实验，并分析结果。”

验证：
- Planner。
- Research Agent。
- Math Agent。
- Architect Agent。
- Coding Agent。
- Experiment Agent。
- Reviewer Agent。

复杂任务必须真实调用 Provider、真实执行工具、真实产生文件。

必须能在中途重启 Core 后继续执行。

## 实验数据

每次实验保存：

- Run ID
- Provider
- Model ID
- Execution Mode
- Model Calls
- Tool Calls
- Token Usage
- Duration
- Retry Count
- Review Results
- Artifact Hashes
- Final Status

真实模型实验与 Mock 实验分开统计。

失败实验必须保留。

---

# 十、算法研究：不要只做工程拼装

FORGE 有三个值得深入的自主研究方向：

1. Capability-Aware Dynamic Team Composition。
2. Evidence-Driven Autonomous Governance。
3. Task-Centric Context Compression。

本轮建立真正可复现的 Benchmark。

重点：

### Team Composition
比较：
- Single Model
- Static Team
- Greedy Selection
- Capability Coverage
- Complementarity
- Dynamic Recomposition

### Context Compression
比较：
- Full Context
- Recency Truncation
- Conventional Summary
- Task-Centric Compression
- Task-Centric Compression + Source Recall

### Agent Governance
比较：
- Model Claim Only
- Tool Receipt Verification
- Independent Reviewer
- Evidence-Gated Completion

至少建立多个不同难度和领域的任务。

使用固定测试集、统一预算和独立评分。

报告成功率、成本、延迟、Token、返工次数和证据完整率。

小样本结果必须明确标记为探索性实验，不允许夸大统计结论。

---

# 十一、本轮明确不做的事情

暂时不投入主要开发资源于：

- UI 视觉重构。
- Tauri 安装包优化。
- NSIS 发布。
- 动画效果。
- 桌面端页面扩展。
- 非必要的数据库重构。

现有桌面端保持可用即可。

如果发现会阻塞 Agent 运行的底层缺陷，可以修复，但不要将桌面测试变成主线。

---

# 十二、执行顺序

请连续执行以下阶段，不需要每个阶段都等待用户确认：

Sprint A：Provider 和 Agent Loop 深度审计及真实调用。

Sprint B：Persistent Router + Planner 智能化。

Sprint C：Dynamic Team Intelligence。

Sprint D：Native Worker 自主执行与自我修正。

Sprint E：Independent Reviewer 与返工闭环。

Sprint F：Context Compaction + Long-term Memory。

Sprint G：Agent Communication Protocol + 故障恢复。

Sprint H：真实复杂任务端到端验收。

Sprint I：三项核心算法 Benchmark 与消融实验。

每个阶段必须有独立测试和可复现报告。

如果发现现有架构不支持目标，应先提出最小必要架构调整，并通过 ADR 记录，不要推倒重写。

---

# 十三、工程约束

1. 保持一个长期用户对话入口。
2. Router 是唯一面向用户的 Agent。
3. Worker 是真正的后台执行 Agent。
4. 不允许通过创建多个用户 Conversation 规避上下文问题。
5. 不允许把 Codex、DSH 或 Claude Code 当作执行后端。
6. 不允许使用伪造的执行记录。
7. 不允许把 Mock 结果标记为 Live。
8. 不允许绕过 Approval、Policy 和 Evidence。
9. 不允许无限 Agent 派生。
10. 不允许无限重试。
11. 不允许无预算模型调用。
12. 保留历史测试和审计证据。
13. 不自动推送或合并 GitHub。
14. 不删除用户原有数据和实验记录。

可以使用多个 Codex 子任务并行分析和实现，但必须指定唯一集成负责人，避免多人同时修改相同核心文件。

---

# 十四、最终交付标准

最终必须让 FORGE 能够：

1. 长期与用户保持同一个对话。
2. 理解用户复杂目标。
3. 自动生成 Quest。
4. 自动规划 DAG。
5. 从模型库选择模型。
6. 动态组建 Agent 团队。
7. 后台并行执行任务。
8. Agent 之间结构化协作。
9. 自动发现错误并修复。
10. Reviewer 独立检查结果。
11. 不合格任务自动返工。
12. 上下文压缩后恢复工作。
13. 长期记忆跨任务复用。
14. Core 重启后继续执行。
15. 所有成果具备可信证据。

生成：

`docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md`

`docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md`

`docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md`

`docs/audit/phase2/verification.json`

{"i":0,"result":{"chunk_id":"74235c","wall_time_seconds":0.6521267,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":4387,"output":"# FORGE — Agent Intelligence Sprint
## Phase 2: From Agent Infrastructure to Autonomous Intelligence

你现在正式进入 FORGE 的下一阶段开发。

本轮不以桌面端发布为目标，而是以真正跑通自主多智能体系统为目标。

用户已经授权你使用本地配置的 Provider。你可以使用现有 Provider 进行真实模型调用、协议测试、Agent 实验和端到端任务验证。

本轮必须把重心从基础设施转移到 Agent Intelligence。

不要继续大规模开发 UI，不要优先处理安装包和 Tauri 外观问题。

核心任务是让 FORGE 真正成为一个能够长期自主工作的 Agent 系统。

---

# 一、首先重新审计当前代码

当前开发分支：

`codex/phase1-continuous`

先读取：

- docs/STATUS.md
- docs/ROADMAP.md
- docs/QUALITY_GATES.md
- docs/PRODUCT_ARCHITECTURE.md
- docs/ROUTER_AND_WORKER_PROTOCOL.md
- docs/MODEL_REGISTRY_AND_TEAM_COMPOSITION.md
- docs/CONTEXT_MEMORY_GOVERNANCE.md
- 所有 Phase 1 Milestone 报告

重点阅读源码：

- forge_core/router.py
- forge_core/worker_runtime.py
- forge_core/team_composition.py
- forge_core/quest_graph.py
- forge_core/dispatcher.py
- forge_core/context_service.py
- forge_core/memory.py
- forge_core/providers/
- forge_core/tool_engine.py
- forge_core/evidence.py
- forge_core/governance.py

先建立一份真正的 Agent 执行链路图。

区分：
1. 已经真实实现的功能。
2. 通过 Mock 验证的功能。
3. 已经通过真实 Provider 验证的功能。
4. 只有接口或数据模型的功能。
5. 目前无法端到端工作的功能。

不要重新实现已经完成的模块。

不要为了让报告好看而隐藏已有缺陷。

审计完成后直接进入开发，不需要等待用户再次批准。

# 二、本地 Provider：正式启用真实模型

用户已经允许使用本地 Provider。

要求：

1. 检查 FORGE 当前 Provider 配置。
2. 检查本地 Provider 服务是否可用。
3. 获取可用模型列表。
4. 检查模型的 Tool Calling、Structured Output、Streaming 能力。
5. 检查模型实际上下文和输出限制。
6. 检查 Token 预算和并发限制。
7. 运行真实模型的最小对话测试。
8. 运行真实模型的 Router 决策测试。
9. 运行真实 Worker 工具调用测试。

如果本地 Provider 是 OpenAI-compatible 服务，优先使用现有 Adapter。

不要新建一套绕过 Gateway 的 Provider 实现。

安全要求：

- 不要打印 API Key。
- 不要把凭据写入源码、日志、Git 或实验报告。
- 不要读取与 FORGE Provider 配置无关的个人文件。
- 不要修改用户原有 Provider 服务配置。
- 不要自动增加无限 Token 预算。
- 不要将 Mock 响应标记为真实模型结果。

如果某个模型不支持 Tool Calling，应该由 Router 选择兼容模型或采用安全的结构化调用适配方案，不要假设所有模型都具备相同能力。

本地 Provider 可能是代理服务，必须区分：
- FORGE 到本地代理的请求成功。
- 上游真实模型调用成功。
- 模型实际返回正确结果。

三者不能混为一谈。

# 三、核心任务：升级 Persistent Router

当前 Router 已经具备模型驱动决策基础，但还需要进一步增强。

目标：

Router 不应该只是一个分类器，而应该成为一个长期存在的自主 Agent。

## 3.1 Router Agent Loop

实现完整的循环：

Observe
→ Understand
→ Retrieve
→ Reason
→ Decide
→ Act
→ Observe Result
→ Reflect
→ Continue

Router 必须具备：

- 持续理解用户目标。
- 自动关联历史 Quest。
- 判断是否创建新 Quest。
- 判断是否继续现有 Quest。
- 识别用户约束。
- 识别任务优先级。
- 识别阻塞条件。
- 根据执行结果调整计划。
- 主动决定何时请求用户帮助。
- 在适当时机主动汇报进展。

不要把所有推理都写成固定 Prompt。

需要建立结构化决策协议，并对模型输出进行严格校验。

## 3.2 Router 与 Planner 分离

Router 负责：
- 用户意图理解。
- 任务生命周期管理。
- Quest 选择。
- 团队协调。
- 结果汇总。
- 用户交互。

Planner 负责：
- 目标分析。
- 子任务拆解。
- DAG 生成。
- 依赖关系推导。
- 成功标准定义。
- 任务执行顺序优化。

Planner 可以作为后台专用 Agent，但不能取代 Router。

## 3.3 复杂任务识别

支持：
- 普通聊天。
- 单步骤执行。
- 多步骤任务。
- 长期研究任务。
- 软件开发任务。
- 多模态任务。
- 多 Quest 并行任务。

不要为了增加 Agent 数量而把简单问题拆成复杂任务。

简单任务应该直接回答。

复杂任务才启动团队。

---

# 四、Dynamic Team Intelligence

这是 FORGE 最重要的创新方向之一。

目前已经具备模型注册、角色合同和基础组队算法。

接下来需要让团队真正根据任务需求动态形成。

## 4.1 Model Intelligence

完善模型画像：

- Coding
- Mathematics
- Research
- Architecture
- Planning
- Design
- Vision
- Writing
- Tool Calling
- Instruction Following

增加实际线上表现：

- Task Success Rate
- Tool Call Success Rate
- Retry Rate
- Schema Compliance
- Average Latency
- P95 Latency
- Token Consumption
- Cost
- Review Pass Rate

注意：

能力评分必须有来源、样本数、测试时间和置信度。

真实数据与用户手动评分分开保存。

不能把一次成功调用直接当成模型能力评分。

## 4.2 Dynamic Team Composer

Router 将 Quest 交给 Composer。

Composer 根据：

- Task Requirements
- Model Capabilities
- Model Reliability
- Tool Compatibility
- Token Budget
- Time Budget
- Coordination Overhead

选择团队。

支持：

- Single Agent
- Sequential Team
- Parallel Team
- Hierarchical Team
- Specialist Team
- Dynamic Expansion

要求模型与角色彻底解耦。

一个模型可以承担多个角色，一个角色也可以根据任务动态切换模型。

## 4.3 团队自适应

执行过程中：

- Worker 可以请求帮助。
- Router 可以增加专家。
- Router 可以替换表现不佳的模型。
- Router 可以重新分配未完成节点。
- Reviewer 可以要求返工。
- Planner 可以重新规划剩余 DAG。

但已完成节点、历史证据和已执行的外部动作不能因为重组而丢失。

团队规模、派生深度、预算和重试次数必须有界。

---

# 五、真正的 Native Worker Agent Loop

不要只把 Worker 当作任务执行函数。

Worker 必须拥有自己的推理循环和工作上下文。

完整过程：

接收任务
→ 理解任务合同
→ 检索必要上下文
→ 选择工具
→ 请求模型
→ 执行工具
→ 读取结果
→ 判断是否完成
→ 必要时修正
→ 输出结构化结果
→ 提交证据
→ 通知 Router

## 5.1 Worker 类型

完善以下角色：

Research Agent：
- 检索资料。
- 整理来源。
- 分析相关工作。
- 提供研究结论。

Math Agent：
- 数学推导。
- 公式验证。
- 数值计算。
- 检查推理漏洞。

Architect Agent：
- 设计系统架构。
- 定义接口。
- 分析依赖。
- 检查技术风险。

Coding Agent：
- 阅读代码。
- 编写代码。
- 修改代码。
- 运行测试。
- 修复错误。

Experiment Agent：
- 设计实验。
- 执行实验。
- 记录结果。
- 生成可复现报告。

Reviewer Agent：
- 检查成果。
- 对照成功标准。
- 检查证据。
- 给出通过或返工决定。

Planner Agent：
- 拆解任务。
- 更新 DAG。
- 管理依赖。
- 处理失败后的重新规划。

## 5.2 Worker 自我修正

Worker 不能遇到错误就直接失败。

应该能够：

1. 读取错误信息。
2. 判断错误类型。
3. 分析可能原因。
4. 选择修复策略。
5. 再次执行。
6. 对比修复前后的结果。
7. 判断是否需要求助。

区分：
- 代码错误。
- 工具错误。
- Provider 错误。
- 任务理解错误。
- 预算耗尽。
- 依赖阻塞。
- 外部资源不可用。

不同错误采用不同恢复策略。

禁止无限循环。

## 5.3 Worker 交付协议

每个 Worker 必须提交：

- Summary
- Findings
- Decisions
- Artifacts
- Evidence References
- Unresolved Issues
- Confidence
- Next Actions

不能只返回一段自由文本。

---

# 六、Reviewer：建立真正的独立审查机制

Reviewer 不应该只是让另一个模型重新总结一次结果。

它必须检查：

1. 是否完成原始目标。
2. 是否满足成功标准。
3. 是否存在未经验证的假设。
4. 产物是否真实存在。
5. 产物是否与执行记录对应。
6. 测试是否真实运行。
7. 是否存在逻辑错误。
8. 是否存在明显遗漏。
9. 是否存在安全问题。

Reviewer 应当拥有独立的上下文。

不要将 Coding Agent 的全部内部推理直接复制给 Reviewer。

Reviewer 应获得：
- 原始任务合同。
- 成功标准。
- 实际产物。
- 可信工具回执。
- 必要的研究来源。
- 测试结果。

审查结果：

PASS
NEEDS_REVISION
REJECT
BLOCKED

NEEDS_REVISION 必须能够创建有明确修改目标的返工任务。

设置最大审查轮次。

Reviewer 不能通过模型自述或 Mock 证据判定成功。

---

# 七、Context Compaction 与 Memory 深度增强

目前 M6 已经实现了有界 Context Archive、Recall 和预算管理。

但长期单一对话仍然有容量边界。

本轮重点解决这个问题。

## 7.1 Task-Centric Compaction

不要简单按时间截断历史。

采用多层上下文：

L0：Recent Interaction
L1：Active Quest Context
L2：Project Memory
L3：Long-term Experience

保留：
- 原始用户目标。
- 用户明确约束。
- 重要决策。
- 已完成节点。
- 当前阻塞。
- 产物路径。
- 证据来源。
- 失败经验。
- 后续行动。

每个压缩摘要必须保留来源引用。

压缩后必须能恢复到原始证据。

## 7.2 解决历史消息无限增长

不要为了保存所有用户约束而无限注入原始消息。

建立约束抽取和引用机制：

- 将用户约束单独索引。
- 保留原始消息 ID。
- 生成有来源的结构化 Constraint Record。
- 检测约束冲突。
- 检测约束是否过期。
- 必要时重新读取原始消息。

模型抽取出的约束先标记为待验证。

用户明确确认的约束与模型推测严格区分。

## 7.3 Memory Retrieval

改进 Recall：

- 语义检索。
- 关键词检索。
- Quest 关联检索。
- 时间检索。
- 来源可靠性过滤。
- 冲突检测。
- 过期过滤。

建立 Retrieval Evaluation Dataset。

测试 Router 是否能准确找到历史 Quest、决策、文件和用户约束。

不要只根据摘要文本相似度判断召回成功。

---

# 八、Agent 之间的协作机制

建立正式的 Agent Communication Protocol。

不允许把自由文本群聊作为主要协调机制。

支持：

TASK_ASSIGNMENT
TASK_ACCEPTED
TASK_COMPLETED
HELP_REQUEST
REVIEW_REQUEST
REVISION_REQUEST
DEPENDENCY_BLOCKED
MODEL_UNAVAILABLE
BUDGET_WARNING
AGENT_FAILED

重要消息持久化。

Router 负责协调。

Worker 不能绕过 Router 自行修改其他 Worker 的任务。

对于跨 Worker 共享的产物，必须通过有权限的 Artifact 和 Receipt 接口访问。

---

# 九、真正跑通复杂任务

本轮必须新增真实端到端实验。

不要只写单元测试。

建立三种任务难度：

## Level 1：简单任务

例如：

“分析这个 Python 项目，指出三个最值得优先修复的问题。”

验证：
- Router 判断。
- Quest 创建。
- 单 Worker 执行。
- 结果回传。

## Level 2：多 Agent 协作

例如：

“调研一个开源 Agent 框架，比较其架构，写一份技术分析报告。”

验证：
- Research Agent。
- Architect Agent。
- Coding/Writer Agent。
- Reviewer Agent。
- Router 汇总。

## Level 3：复杂自主开发

例如：

“研究一个新的 Agent 算法，提出技术方案，实现实验代码，运行实验，并分析结果。”

验证：
- Planner。
- Research Agent。
- Math Agent。
- Architect Agent。
- Coding Agent。
- Experiment Agent。
- Reviewer Agent。

复杂任务必须真实调用 Provider、真实执行工具、真实产生文件。

必须能在中途重启 Core 后继续执行。

## 实验数据

每次实验保存：

- Run ID
- Provider
- Model ID
- Execution Mode
- Model Calls
- Tool Calls
- Token Usage
- Duration
- Retry Count
- Review Results
- Artifact Hashes
- Final Status

真实模型实验与 Mock 实验分开统计。

失败实验必须保留。

---

# 十、算法研究：不要只做工程拼装

FORGE 有三个值得深入的自主研究方向：

1. Capability-Aware Dynamic Team Composition。
2. Evidence-Driven Autonomous Governance。
3. Task-Centric Context Compression。

本轮建立真正可复现的 Benchmark。

重点：

### Team Composition
比较：
- Single Model
- Static Team
- Greedy Selection
- Capability Coverage
- Complementarity
- Dynamic Recomposition

### Context Compression
比较：
- Full Context
- Recency Truncation
- Conventional Summary
- Task-Centric Compression
- Task-Centric Compression + Source Recall

### Agent Governance
比较：
- Model Claim Only
- Tool Receipt Verification
- Independent Reviewer
- Evidence-Gated Completion

至少建立多个不同难度和领域的任务。

使用固定测试集、统一预算和独立评分。

报告成功率、成本、延迟、Token、返工次数和证据完整率。

小样本结果必须明确标记为探索性实验，不允许夸大统计结论。

---

# 十一、本轮明确不做的事情

暂时不投入主要开发资源于：

- UI 视觉重构。
- Tauri 安装包优化。
- NSIS 发布。
- 动画效果。
- 桌面端页面扩展。
- 非必要的数据库重构。

现有桌面端保持可用即可。

如果发现会阻塞 Agent 运行的底层缺陷，可以修复，但不要将桌面测试变成主线。

---

# 十二、执行顺序

请连续执行以下阶段，不需要每个阶段都等待用户确认：

Sprint A：Provider 和 Agent Loop 深度审计及真实调用。

Sprint B：Persistent Router + Planner 智能化。

Sprint C：Dynamic Team Intelligence。

Sprint D：Native Worker 自主执行与自我修正。

Sprint E：Independent Reviewer 与返工闭环。

Sprint F：Context Compaction + Long-term Memory。

Sprint G：Agent Communication Protocol + 故障恢复。

Sprint H：真实复杂任务端到端验收。

Sprint I：三项核心算法 Benchmark 与消融实验。

每个阶段必须有独立测试和可复现报告。

如果发现现有架构不支持目标，应先提出最小必要架构调整，并通过 ADR 记录，不要推倒重写。

---

# 十三、工程约束

1. 保持一个长期用户对话入口。
2. Router 是唯一面向用户的 Agent。
3. Worker 是真正的后台执行 Agent。
4. 不允许通过创建多个用户 Conversation 规避上下文问题。
5. 不允许把 Codex、DSH 或 Claude Code 当作执行后端。
6. 不允许使用伪造的执行记录。
7. 不允许把 Mock 结果标记为 Live。
8. 不允许绕过 Approval、Policy 和 Evidence。
9. 不允许无限 Agent 派生。
10. 不允许无限重试。
11. 不允许无预算模型调用。
12. 保留历史测试和审计证据。
13. 不自动推送或合并 GitHub。
14. 不删除用户原有数据和实验记录。

可以使用多个 Codex 子任务并行分析和实现，但必须指定唯一集成负责人，避免多人同时修改相同核心文件。

---

# 十四、最终交付标准

最终必须让 FORGE 能够：

1. 长期与用户保持同一个对话。
2. 理解用户复杂目标。
3. 自动生成 Quest。
4. 自动规划 DAG。
5. 从模型库选择模型。
6. 动态组建 Agent 团队。
7. 后台并行执行任务。
8. Agent 之间结构化协作。
9. 自动发现错误并修复。
10. Reviewer 独立检查结果。
11. 不合格任务自动返工。
12. 上下文压缩后恢复工作。
13. 长期记忆跨任务复用。
14. Core 重启后继续执行。
15. 所有成果具备可信证据。

生成：

`docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md`

`docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md`

# Product Architecture

## Product definition

FORGE is a goal-driven, persistent-router autonomous Agent system. Its primary interface is one continuous conversation. The user does not open or switch task sessions to work with different Agents.

## User-facing continuity versus internal concurrency

The product intentionally separates the conversational surface from execution concurrency:

- **Conversation**: the stable user-visible timeline.
- **Router**: the persistent user-facing Agent identity. It receives all user messages and owns the response.
- **Quest**: a durable objective inferred or explicitly requested by the user.
- **Task Node**: a unit of work inside a Quest DAG.
- **Worker Session**: a private, isolated execution context assigned to one or more task nodes.
- **Event**: a durable fact about state transition, progress, request, result or failure.

A single conversation can contain multiple simultaneous Quests. The Router resolves follow-up references using active Quest state, recency, project context and explicit user references. If ambiguity is material, it asks one concise clarification rather than silently attaching a message to the wrong Quest.

## Router responsibilities

1. Maintain conversational continuity and the Router Task Capsule.
2. Classify each message as chat, create, continue, update, status or approval.
3. Resolve the target Quest.
4. Plan and maintain Quest DAGs.
5. Compose a team from model capability profiles and role contracts.
6. Request approval under Review autonomy.
7. Dispatch hidden Worker Sessions.
8. Consume Worker events and decide which ones merit user-facing delivery.
9. Replan on blocker, failure, evidence gap or changed user goal.
10. Produce one coherent user-facing response.

The Router is not a monolithic prompt with an ever-growing transcript. It operates over bounded recent turns, a compact capsule, Quest state, event cursor and retrieved evidence.

## Worker visibility policy

Worker sessions are hidden by default. The UI may show a task/activity panel with Worker role, state, progress summary and artifacts, but never exposes each Worker as a separate chat that the user must manage.

Workers send structured messages:
- `accepted`
- `progress`
- `help_requested`
- `blocked`
- `artifact_ready`
- `review_requested`
- `completed`
- `failed`

The Router decides whether to surface an event immediately, batch it, or wait for the final result. Important blockers and approvals are surfaced immediately. Routine progress can be coalesced to avoid spamming the conversation.

## Model intelligence

The Model Registry is a resource catalog, not a role catalog. A model can serve many roles; a role can be assigned to different models. Capability scores must carry provenance, sample count, timestamp and confidence. Unknown is not zero and must not be fabricated.

## Reference implementation boundaries

DSH/Super-agent informs persistent Router, hidden Workers, durable task routing and event handoff. Codex informs harness boundaries, event-oriented execution, tool safety and context compaction. Claude Code public documentation informs subagent contracts, hooks and permission concepts. FORGE implements its own runtime and data model rather than shelling out to these products.
# Router, Quest and Worker Protocol

## Core loop

1. Load a bounded snapshot of RouterState, recent turns, Quest summaries and events.
2. Call the configured Provider outside the database write transaction for a structured decision.
3. Validate the decision and resolve Quest references; ask the user when multiple targets remain plausible.
4. Commit the user message, decision effects, response and applicable cursor changes atomically after version checks.
5. Authenticated user approval is required for governed actions; model output cannot grant it.

M4–M5 implement durable DAG scheduling, Worker event consumption and the native Worker Loop. Mock protocol tests remain distinct from real provider demonstrations; the current real JSON completion demonstration proves syntax validation only. Chain-of-Recall memory remains M6 work. Worker help creates a durable Router composition request and a pending team proposal; no model event grants approval.

## Message envelope

Every internal message should include:
- `message_id`
- `conversation_id`
- `quest_id` (nullable)
- `task_node_id` (nullable)
- `sender_type` and `sender_id`
- `message_type`
- `correlation_id`
- `payload`
- `created_at`

## Event envelope

Events are append-only and sequence-numbered. Consumers must be idempotent. Event delivery is at-least-once; handlers record their last processed sequence. Do not assume exactly-once delivery.

## Router-to-Worker messages

`ASSIGN_TASK`, `CANCEL_TASK`, `PAUSE_TASK`, `RESUME_TASK`, `REQUEST_STATUS`, `REQUEST_REVISION`.

## Worker-to-Router messages

`ACCEPTED`, `PROGRESS`, `HELP_REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`, `ARTIFACT_READY`, `REVIEW_REQUESTED`, `RESULT`, `FAILED`.

## Notification policy

- Immediate: approval needed, blocked, destructive-risk warning, user clarification needed, final result.
- Coalesced: routine progress, repeated tool status, heartbeat.
- Silent by default: internal reasoning, raw chain-of-thought, low-level polling.
- Never expose hidden Worker private reasoning. Surface concise status, decisions and evidence.

## Quest resolution

Resolution priority:
1. Explicit Quest ID or task card reference.
2. Direct semantic match against active Quest title/goal and recent conversation.
3. Ask clarification if multiple plausible targets remain; do not guess a current Quest.

Do not attach an unrelated new request to the most recently active Quest just because it is recent.
# Model Registry and Dynamic Team Composition

## Model Profile dimensions

Identity: provider, model_id, display_name, version, endpoint, enabled.
Capabilities: reasoning, math, coding, architecture, research, writing, design, vision, tool_use, instruction_following.
Performance: TTFT, tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, reliability, timeout rate.
Economics: input/output/cache price, currency, updated timestamp.
Limits: context window, max output, rate limits, concurrency.
Features: streaming, tool calls, JSON mode, image/audio/video input.
Provenance: provider metadata, FORGE benchmark, online observations, user override.
Uncertainty: sample_count, measured_at, confidence interval or confidence label.

Never fabricate model capabilities or pricing. Provider metadata may be unavailable; retain `unknown`.

## Benchmark dimensions
- Math: answer correctness and proof/derivation rubric.
- Coding: tests, hidden tests, patch correctness and regression.
- Planning: dependency completeness, feasibility, rework rate.
- Research: source validity, coverage and factual consistency.
- Tool use: schema accuracy, success and policy compliance.
- Design: visual tasks, constraint coverage and human blind review; text-only self-ratings are insufficient.
- Speed: real TTFT and generation speed measurements.
- Cost: observed usage multiplied by verified price metadata.

## Role Template
A role defines objective, responsibilities, input contract, output schema, required capabilities, allowed tools, risk class, context budget and acceptance criteria. It must not hard-bind one provider/model.

## Team composition
Initial explainable baseline:
1. Filter enabled, healthy models compatible with modality/tool requirements.
2. Score task fit using capability profiles with confidence weighting.
3. Apply cost, latency, context and concurrency constraints.
4. Select role coverage and penalize redundant capabilities/coordination overhead.
5. Return top candidates and explain selection.
6. In Review mode, ask the user to approve the plan/team.

Later research: constrained set selection, complementarity, online routing and dynamic re-composition. Compare against single-best-model and fixed-team baselines.

## M5 implementation and evidence

The current bounded composer implements single_model, greedy, coverage and complementarity strategies with capability provenance/confidence, context/output, exact tool scope, token, currency/cost and concurrency constraints. Unknown measurements remain unknown. Eight preset roles coexist with complete, bounded dynamic contracts; every approved DAG node has one member. Model identity never grants permissions.

Team approval binds the exact plan and selected profile hashes. Worker help can request a separately approved replacement; only settled unfinished assignments may be replaced, with at most three replacements per Quest and no budget refund. Completed nodes retain their original run and historical approval evidence. Execution requires a current approved team; a separate verifier-only historical lookup permits proved superseded approvals, excludes revoked contracts and checks run creation against approval/supersession time.

The synthetic-team-v2 experiment compares four strategies and confidence/coordination ablations on three fixed scenarios. It measures selection mechanics, not real provider task quality. See [M5 report](PHASE1_MILESTONE5_REPORT.md) for actual results and limitations.
# Context, Memory, Governance and Evidence

## Context Compaction
The system must preserve task continuity, not merely summarize chat. A Task Capsule includes goal, success criteria, confirmed facts with evidence refs, hypotheses with status, decisions, completed/pending steps, blockers, constraints, artifacts, next action and source event cursor.

Compaction:
1. Snapshot authoritative state and recent events.
2. Generate structured capsule.
3. Validate required fields and references.
4. Archive old messages rather than destroying them.
5. Rebuild context from policy + capsule + relevant evidence + recent turns.
6. Record token counts, compaction version and recovery checks.

## Chain of Recall
Router recall indexes Quests, decisions, artifacts and evidence. Every recalled fact includes source and freshness. Distinguish verified facts from model hypotheses. On conflict, prefer newer verified evidence and surface uncertainty.

### M6 implementation in progress

The Core derives a project source from the bound Workspace, Task sources from
Quest records, decision and failure sources from a fixed set of Core events, and
artifact sources from trusted evidence records. Working context remains the
unarchived Session messages; Quest records are L1, the Workspace source is L2,
and failure experience is L3. Event payloads and evidence remain hypotheses
about their content: a trusted record establishes that Core recorded an event or
verification at that time, not the truth of a domain claim or the current state
of a file. The public memory write interface rejects a caller's attempt to label
an arbitrary claim confirmed. A recall result identifies sources, timestamps,
freshness, conflicts and related Quests; unknown freshness remains unknown.

Source indexing is incremental and transactional. Event, Quest and evidence
cursors advance with the derived index; source snapshots are hashed and checked
against current Core rows and plan revisions on read. Revoked sources are
excluded. Each synchronization processes a bounded batch and reports whether
more work remains. Retrieval uses indexed terms and a bounded candidate page;
its cursor and omission count signal incomplete results and must not be treated
as proof that an omitted Quest does not exist. Candidate ambiguity must remain
visible to the Router. This is still under integration and acceptance; see
[current status](STATUS.md) and the [synthetic study](PHASE1_MILESTONE6_CONTEXT_EXPERIMENT.md).

Only evidence with a recorded plan revision is indexed as a plan-bound source.
The general `ArtifactVerifier` can create records without that revision; these
are indexed as historical, explicitly unbound observations and cannot establish
the current plan's completion or the present contents of a file. Events without
a resolvable plan revision are skipped rather than assigned the Quest's current
revision. The index is derived data and is not an authorization or
task-completion authority.

## Governance
Default Review mode. Policy engine, not model, grants permissions. Risk levels:
- R0 read-only analysis.
- R1 reversible writes inside approved workspace.
- R2 external side effects or shared resource mutation.
- R3 deletion, credential access, payment, production action.
R3 defaults to deny or explicit secondary confirmation.

Approval is bound to a specific plan/action and parameter digest. Agent cannot elevate its own permissions. Budgets cover tokens, cost, time, tool calls and concurrency.

## Evidence
Task completion requires evidence from trusted tools or independent verification. Model claims are not evidence. Test evidence records command, environment, exit code, report path and timestamp. Evidence graph links Task, Worker, ToolCall, Artifact, TestRun, Decision and Approval.

**Milestone 7 实施中，尚未验收。** 用户已暂缓桌面验收，本轮聚焦后端加固；进展及待验项见[后端加固报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md)。单一持久聊天、桌面 Core 生命周期、设置、审批与权限范围、凭据及备份恢复仍需最终集成验证。Windows 安装包、完整原生联调和有界 Alpha 场景须以最终冻结版本的实际结果为准；早期隔离启动和 Mock 浏览器测试不代表发布通过。总体进展见 [M7 报告草稿](PHASE1_MILESTONE7_REPORT.md)。

本轮后端加固已完成本机验证：冻结快照完整测试 **488 passed，1 warning，107.62 秒**；双工作目录 Ruff、格式及依赖检查通过，历史文件和原测试保留核验见[验证记录](audit/phase1/milestone7-backend-hardening-verification.json)。六角色审批、Reviewer 与重启的完整 Mock 链以及付费 Alpha 尚未完成。

Milestone 5 的 Native Worker、动态团队、工具治理与独立证据链已完成本机冻结验收：**282 passed，1 warning，44.99 秒**；真实供应商完成有限的 numeric AST 和 JSON 产物演示，范围见 [M5 报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE5_REPORT.md)。Milestone 6 的最终快照本机完整测试为 **372 passed，1 warning，77.78 秒**，静态、依赖与历史证据核验通过；一次有界真实供应商任务恢复成功，前五次诊断失败均保留。有限合成研究及容量边界见 [M6 报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE6_REPORT.md)。这些结果不能证明无限对话或通用任务正确性。

M6 已将 Router、planner、composer、benchmark 和 Worker 的模型请求接入统一 Gateway 准入。价格未知时使用 token-only，不推算费用。当前限制和质量门槛见 [QUALITY_GATES](QUALITY_GATES.md)，配置及恢复复核步骤见 [README](../README.md)。

## 历史阶段与证据

各阶段报告和审计记录保留当时的测试结果、限制和待办，其历史描述不代表当前状态：

- [Phase 0 审计](PHASE0_AUDIT.md)及[验证证据](audit/phase0/verification.json)。
- [Milestone 1](PHASE1_MILESTONE1_REPORT.md)、[Milestone 2](PHASE1_MILESTONE2_REPORT.md)、[Milestone 3](PHASE1_MILESTONE3_REPORT.md) 和 [Milestone 4](PHASE1_MILESTONE4_REPORT.md) 报告。
- [Milestone 5](PHASE1_MILESTONE5_REPORT.md) 和 [Milestone 6](PHASE1_MILESTONE6_REPORT.md) 报告及各自审计证据。

历史审计脚本可能覆盖历史证据，重跑前应使用独立输出位置。阶段路线及尚未验证的验收目标见 [ROADMAP](ROADMAP.md)。
# Detailed Implementation Roadmap

## Continuous engineering milestones — 2026-11-15

- Milestone 1：数据可靠性本机验证完成，历史交付保留。
- Milestone 2：治理、Core 本地信任边界、证据门槛基础及依赖锁通过阶段审查；当时的范围见 [报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE2_REPORT.md)。
- Milestone 3：Provider Gateway、Persistent Router 和模型画像基础完成本机 Mock 协议测试；当时的范围见 [报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE3_REPORT.md)。后续有限真实供应商验证见 M5、M6 报告。
- Milestone 4：Quest Graph、事件投递和应用生命周期接线已完成本机 Mock/SQLite 验证，详见 [报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE4_REPORT.md)。
- Milestone 5：Native Worker、动态团队、固定工具治理与可信执行证据已完成本机冻结验收（282 项测试）；真实供应商通过有限的数值与 JSON 产物演示，范围见 [报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE5_REPORT.md)。
- Milestone 6：Context 归档、来源 Recall 与 Gateway 模型调用统一预算通过本机验证（372 passed）；真实供应商一次有界连续任务恢复成功，前五次诊断失败保留。容量和范围见 [报告](PHASE1_MILESTONE6_REPORT.md)。
- Milestone 7：桌面 Alpha 与 Tauri Core 生命周期正在集成；早期隔离原生启动已观察，最终原生联调、安装包和 Alpha 验收仍待完成。见 [报告草稿](PHASE1_MILESTONE7_REPORT.md)。

以下是原始目标清单，保留作为功能范围参考，而非当前完成状态的逐项核对；它的 Phase 编号与上述连续开发 Milestone 编号不同。具体已验证范围和剩余限制以上述报告及 [STATUS](STATUS.md) 为准。

## Phase 0 — Engineering audit
- [ ] Inspect Python/Node/Rust/Tauri toolchain and repository.
- [ ] Run tests and frontend build.
- [ ] Create ADRs and architecture guardrails.
- [ ] Confirm local startup scripts and deterministic DB location.
- [ ] Add CI workflow and static checks.
- [ ] Record real results in STATUS.
Acceptance: clean environment can start API/UI; tests pass.

## Phase 1 — Persistent Router
- [ ] Replace heuristic classifier with provider-backed Router Agent Loop.
- [ ] Define structured RouterAction schema.
- [ ] Implement intent and Quest reference resolution.
- [ ] Persist Router capsule and event cursor.
- [ ] Implement one unified conversation timeline.
- [ ] Ensure restart recovery.
Acceptance: multiple different topics and concurrent Quests remain in one user-visible conversation.

## Phase 2 — Quest Graph and event relay
- [ ] Add TaskNode, dependencies, cycle checks and DAG scheduler.
- [ ] Add worker event inbox/outbox and idempotent consumers.
- [ ] Add progress coalescing and important-event direct delivery.
- [ ] Add Quest pause/resume/cancel/update.
Acceptance: Worker progress/results appear in the same conversation; no separate user chat.

## Phase 3 — Model Registry
- [ ] Provider adapters for OpenAI-compatible and native APIs.
- [ ] Secure OS credential vault.
- [ ] Provider model discovery where supported.
- [ ] Benchmark task definitions and versioning.
- [ ] Benchmark runner and provenance.
- [ ] Online performance statistics and user override.
Acceptance: at least two real providers and auditable capability profiles.

## Phase 4 — Native Runtime and tools
- [ ] Streaming model gateway and retry/error mapping.
- [ ] Agent Loop and structured tool-call parser.
- [ ] Tool schemas and policy enforcement.
- [ ] Sandboxed file and command tools.
- [ ] Worker session persistence, cancellation and recovery.
Acceptance: a Worker performs a bounded multi-step task using native runtime.

## Phase 5 — Dynamic Team Composer
- [ ] Role templates and bounded dynamic role synthesis.
- [ ] Capability/confidence scoring.
- [ ] Cost/latency/context/concurrency constraints.
- [ ] Complementarity and coordination penalty.
- [ ] Explainable team proposals and approval.
- [ ] Dynamic re-composition on failure/blocker.
Acceptance: Router builds and explains a suitable team for distinct task types.

## Phase 6 — Context and Chain of Recall
- [ ] Task Capsule and compaction trigger.
- [ ] Archive and restore conversation context.
- [ ] Quest/project memory and evidence-linked retrieval.
- [ ] Memory freshness, contradiction and invalidation.
Acceptance: long task resumes after compaction/restart without losing constraints.

## Phase 7 — Governance and evidence
- [ ] Risk policy and exact-scope approvals.
- [ ] Budget ledger and circuit breakers.
- [ ] Evidence graph and artifact hashes.
- [ ] Independent verification.
Acceptance: unsafe actions blocked; completion supported by evidence.

## Phase 8 — Desktop release
- [ ] Tauri Rust bootstrap and Core lifecycle manager.
- [ ] Single chat with embedded Quest cards.
- [ ] Model Library, Agent activity, Memory and Approval views.
- [ ] OS credential storage, backup/restore and Windows installer.
Acceptance: end-to-end local desktop demo.

## Definition of Done
Every phase includes code, tests, docs, migration, error handling, logs, reproducible demo and STATUS update. No phase is complete based only on code generation.
# Quality Gates and Known Limitations

## Current engineering evidence
- M6 local engineering verification passed: 372 tests, one deprecation warning, Ruff from both working directories, dependency checks and historical-evidence hashes. One bounded real-provider continuation succeeded after five retained diagnostic failures; see the [M6 report](PHASE1_MILESTONE6_REPORT.md).
- M7 desktop lifecycle, settings, backup and UI integration are in progress. Early isolated native startup is not a packaged Alpha or a general correctness result. On the current intermediate source, the desktop's 12 Node tests and TypeScript check passed; npm audit against the official registry reported zero vulnerabilities. A production build emitted its output, but the command has not yet exited and therefore is not counted as a passed build. Final frozen-source checks, installation and the requested Alpha scenario remain pending.
- A Windows Rust dependency audit reported no vulnerabilities but did report two upstream advisories for `proc-macro-error` and `glib`; the native owner reports those packages are outside the Windows target graph. This does not establish safety on other platforms. See the final M7 evidence for the audited graph and exact scope.

## Verified at Milestone 3
- Backend suite: 140 passed, 1 warning; Ruff, pip check and the locked Python dependency audit passed on Windows/Python 3.13.
- Model Provider and Router protocols were exercised with explicitly labelled Mock responses and MockTransport, including local HTTP startup/restart tests. Real provider calls remain unverified.
- See [Milestone 3 report](PHASE1_MILESTONE3_REPORT.md) and [verification evidence](audit/phase1/milestone3-verification.json) for exact commands, results and limitations.

## Still open
- The final packaged Windows application, end-to-end desktop Core lifecycle and M7 Alpha scenario.
- General model quality, unrestricted task correctness, arbitrary-scale continuity and production durability. M5/M6 bounded live and local tests do not prove these claims.
- Final M7 credential vault, backup/restore and native integration acceptance; test credentials must remain dummy and temporary.

## Engineering cautions
- Router decisions are validated and ambiguous targets require clarification. Recall is bounded and signals omitted candidates; the compaction task snapshot is limited to 100 active Quests.
- SQLite has versioned migrations, transaction boundaries and regression tests; this does not establish production durability under every failure mode.
- Team scoring is a simple capability-fit baseline, not the final research algorithm.
- Never describe proposed Worker records as running Workers.
